Daily signatures on kansalaisaloite.fi¶

The question is what in the calendar remains once each initiative has its own level and its own age. The page reads a cached snapshot. Fetching is a separate step (python -m src.fetch), and these cells do not call the network.

Through 2026-10-23, the daily series records 12,048,033 web signatures on 1,937 initiatives. Each date is one count, and the file ends at the nightly cutoff. Initiative 17951 is 1,611 in the series and 1,685 on the counter. Paper and other channels are a total of 677,250 with no dates. The open API has no hour of day and no hour of week.

The 2017 level¶

The upper panel adds every usable initiative. It rises when a large initiative is young and when many are open. The lower panel divides by the number of open initiative-days. A young initiative, or one large month, still moves that rate. The dashed line is 1 January 2017.

Monthly web signatures

The median month has 14.9 signatures per open initiative-day through 2016 (52 full months), 13.1 in 2017 (12 months) and 37.4 from 2018 through 2025 (96 months). The 2017 median sits with the earlier years. The higher level is 2018 onward. In the median month the largest initiative is 31% of the month through 2016, 46% in 2017 and 29% from 2018 through 2025.

The six-month path¶

The left panel is every finished initiative that stayed under 50,000 web signatures and was open at least 170 days (1,316 initiatives, median window 182 days). The line is the median share of that initiative's own web signatures. The band is the middle half.

By day 91 the median has 76%. The middle half runs from 64% to 84%. The logarithm is at 75% that day. A square root of elapsed time, on a 183-day window, is at 71%. A constant daily rate is at 50%. At the end of the first fortnight the median has 22%, the logarithm 23% and the square root 27%.

The logarithm fitted to the median is ln(1 + t/16.8) / ln(1 + 183/16.8). Each curve starts at 0 and ends at 1 on day 183. The offset 16.8 days is fit on ages 7–176. The root-mean-square gap on those days is 0.006 for the logarithm, 0.026 for a fading inflow, 0.032 for elapsed time to the power 0.46, 0.038 for a square root and 0.216 for a constant daily rate. The logarithm has the smallest of these gaps. In the fading inflow each signature still to come is assigned to the remaining days with roughly equal chance, and the daily inflow halves every 50 days. Under the logarithm the daily inflow falls as 1/(t + 16.8). The inflow halves when age and the offset together double, and each doubling adds 28% of the initiative's web signatures. From day 14 on, the logarithm stays within 1.5 percentage points of the median.

The gaps above are for the pointwise median of the cumulative shares. One logarithm for every initiative leaves a median gap of 0.117. Each initiative's own offset brings the median gap to 0.065. Each initiative's own fading inflow leaves a median gap of 0.068. A square root leaves a median gap of 0.126.

The median initiative's own share of its total on days 7, 30, 90 and 150 is 1.05%, 0.50%, 0.21% and 0.13%. Those shares fall as 1/(t + 16.8). On the same days the median line rises by 2.38%, 1.09%, 0.53% and 0.25%. Each of those rises is about twice the share on that day.

One account is a wide spread of discovery times, with similar numbers of people at each doubling of the wait. Another is visibility that thins as the initiative ages. Either account yields an inflow proportional to 1/(t + 16.8), and the median curve has that shape.

The median share on the start date is 0%. The first week holds 9.5%. The first fortnight holds 22%, the second fortnight 11%, and the last fortnight 2.8%. By day 150 the median is 93%.

Initiatives in the slowest quarter of the first week are at 72% by day 91. Initiatives in the fastest quarter are at 85%.

The right panel is the initiatives that reached 50,000 on the web and have finished. 37 initiatives closed before day 170. Their median window is 41 days. After the recorded end the share stays at 1, because collection has stopped. Their median is 98% by day 30. The first fortnight holds 79%, and halfway through their own window they have 79%.

Their median crosses 50,000 on day 23, holding 92% of the signatures they eventually record.

55 initiatives stayed open at least 170 days. At day 91 their median is 45% (middle half 26% to 73%). Their first fortnight holds 16%. Over days 170–183 the median initiative adds 2.3%.

The median share is 22% by day 25, 47% by day 100, 74% by day 150 and 90% by day 160. From day 150 to day 160 the median share rises by 17%. Over those ten days the median initiative adds 2.2%.

Their median crosses 50,000 on day 163, holding 93% of the signatures they eventually record.

Halfway through their own shorter window the early closures have collected 79%. A full six-month initiative that stays under 50,000 has collected 76% by day 91. Same shape, different length of window.

94 initiatives reach 50,000 on the web. Their median crossing is day 116. 3.2% cross on the start date, 18% within seven days and 35% within 30 days. 2 initiatives are still inside their window and already at 50,000 on the web, so they sit in the crossing count. The figure shows finished windows. 13 initiatives of the 107 with a public total of at least 50,000 stay under 50,000 on the web series. The recorded end date is the day collection stopped.

Weekday after day 7¶

From 2017 through the cutoff, after day 7, 1,153 initiatives and 21,963 seven-day blocks. A block that contains a statutory holiday or a named eve is left out. The median gives each initiative-week the same weight. Wednesday is 1.13 (1.11–1.13) times a fair share of that week. Saturday is 0.80 (0.79–0.81). The regression on 1 plus the day's count puts Wednesday at 1.10 (1.09–1.11) and Saturday at 0.86 (0.85–0.86). Thursday is 1.10 (1.09–1.12) in the median initiative-week and 1.05 (0.99–1.15) when weeks are weighted by signatures. Heavy weeks do not single out Thursday the way the typical week does.

Month, week and day of year¶

The multiplier holds the initiative, the week of the initiative and the day inside that week fixed, and it is read on 1 plus the day's count. A value above 1 is a day above the average open day in the sample. The week of the initiative absorbs how young it is, so the month comes from initiatives that reach the same age in different months. The sample is 1,153 initiatives and 193,144 open days from 2017 onward. January is 1.41 (1.35–1.48). June is 0.61 (0.59–0.62).

Holidays and the day of the month¶

A named day is the residual after the initiative, the week of the initiative, the day inside that week, the weekday and the month. The multiplier is on 1 plus the count, against the day the weekday and the month already imply. Below that day: Christmas Eve (jouluaatto) 0.37 (0.34–0.39), Christmas Day (joulupäivä) 0.49 (0.46–0.53), Boxing Day (tapaninpäivä) 0.64 (0.61–0.69), New Year's Day (uudenvuodenpäivä) 0.67 (0.62–0.71), Midsummer eve (juhannusaatto) 0.68 (0.66–0.70), Midsummer Day (juhannuspäivä) 0.69 (0.66–0.71), May Day eve (vappuaatto) 0.77 (0.73–0.82), New Year's Eve (uudenvuodenaatto) 0.91 (0.85–0.98), Epiphany (loppiainen) 0.92 (0.86–0.98) and Easter Monday (2. pääsiäispäivä) 0.95 (0.91–0.98). Above that day: All Saints' Day (pyhäinpäivä) 1.19 (1.12–1.27). Intervals that include 1: Good Friday (pitkäperjantai), Easter Sunday (pääsiäispäivä), May Day (vappu), Ascension (helatorstai) and Independence Day (itsenäisyyspäivä).
